power_for_place.why: B is closer to the supplied benchmarks. A repeatedly reuses both existing Crown stats and newly generated Tribute; its assumed 1.5–2 uses understates succession builds.

A_outliers.issue: Its +3/+3 Tribute across three successors supplies roughly 18 combat stats, versus the T2 median of 6, before buffs.
Four successive inheritances can reuse its incremental Tribute for approximately 20 combat stats: 2×(4+3+2+1), versus 4.5.
Converting a 20/20 king into Crown stats used by three successors yields roughly 80 net combat stats after subtracting the destroyed body, versus 20.
Adds zero stats or keywords. Its relocation often repeats default succession; a 5/5 and occasional repositioning undershoot a strong T4 composition piece.

B_outliers.issue: Nine printed stats, zero added value, and no personal Crowned or Usurp payoff. Weighted eligibility alone scarcely supplies a T4 composition piece.
A 30-Attack king feeding three successors generates at least 90 temporary Attack, versus 42 combat value; accumulated successor Attack can increase this further.

power_for_place.A_tier_jobs: T1–2 establish Tribute; T3 enables succession; T4 mixes explosive conversion with weak relocation; T5 multiplies passes; T6 supplies substantial capstones.
power_for_place.B_tier_jobs: T1–2 establish bodies and buffs; T3 defines crown manipulation; T4 is uneven; T5 supplies direction and protection; T6 expands existing engines.

distinctiveness.why: Body-independent, transferable stats create a more novel resource and decision space than buffing an Attack-selected carry.
distinctiveness.A_core: A reusable throne: preserve, move, convert or cash out its stats.
distinctiveness.B_core: Feeding the strongest minion competes with engineering changes of leadership.

A_has_B_lost: Pretender, Mog'dorg and Treasurer make the Crown convertible storage. Lawgiver controls inheritance; Dentarg separates shop and combat kings. B loses that breadth.
B_has_A_lost: Grog Slinger, Two-Head and Magus make ordinary Attack manipulation govern leadership. Tribute therefore resists Usurp naturally; its once-per-phase cap also bounds repeated rewards. A loses that tension and restraint.
